build_check.description: index.html and game_logic.js exist, a canvas/WebGL renderer is present, and no disallowed heavy runtime asset references are used.

requirements.description: The player character falls continuously downward. Pressing fire shoots a projectile beneath the character, destroying soft blocks and providing upward recoil that slows the fall. The recoil is visible and affects trajectory. Score 0 if no downward shooting or recoil exists.
A combo system tracks consecutive enemy/block kills without landing. The combo counter is visible and multiplies gem value. Landing on a platform resets the combo. Score 0 if no combo system exists.

The player has a health system — touching enemies, spikes, or the top of the screen costs health. Reaching zero health ends the run with a game-over screen. Score 0 if the player is invincible or death has no consequence.

The descent is procedurally generated — each run produces a different arrangement of platforms, enemies, and hazards. No two runs are identical in layout. Score 0 if levels are static and hand-crafted with no variation.

Shop platforms appear periodically during descent offering purchasable upgrades (weapon spread, fire rate, health, shield) for collected gems. At least 3 distinct upgrade options are available. Score 0 if no shop or upgrade system exists.

At least 3 distinct enemy types appear during descent with different movement patterns (horizontal drifters, vertical bouncers, chasers). Different enemies require different avoidance or attack strategies. Score 0 if only one enemy type exists or no enemies are present.

Multiple block/terrain types exist: soft blocks (destroyable), hard blocks (indestructible), hazard blocks (spikes), and gem blocks (drop currency). Each type is visually distinct and behaves differently. Score 0 if only one block type exists.

Depth tiers change the environment theme and difficulty — deeper sections have denser hazards, faster scroll speed, and different visual themes. At least 3 distinct depth tiers are observable. Score 0 if the environment never changes with depth.

The shop offers at least 3 mechanically distinct upgrade categories (weapon modifications, defensive options, utility) that visibly change gameplay after purchase. Score 0 if upgrades are cosmetic only or fewer than 3 categories exist.
A game-over screen shows depth reached, gems collected, max combo achieved, enemies killed, and a retry button. Results reflect actual run performance. Score 0 if no results screen exists.
A styled title screen shows the game name, high score, and Start button with thematic art before gameplay begins. Score 0 if the game starts directly in gameplay or uses raw default UI.
The game flow connects title -> descent gameplay -> shop encounters -> game over -> retry/title without restarting. All transitions are smooth. Score 0 if transitions are missing or require relaunch.
During gameplay, health, gem count, combo counter, and depth meter are visible in a clear HUD that does not obstruct the play area. Score 0 if no HUD is displayed.
Readability at 1280x720 is strong: player, projectiles, enemies, blocks, gems, and hazards are all clearly distinguishable against the background. Score 0 if elements blend together.

The art direction is coherent across title, descent shaft, enemies, blocks, shop, and UI — a consistent vertical-descent aesthetic with unified palette and visual hierarchy. Score 0 if mostly default UI or mismatched placeholders dominate. Full credit may be earned with runtime-authored procedural textures, layered materials, deliberate multi-light rigs, particles, synthesized audio, or post-processing; external asset files are not required.

The descent environment uses real sprite or tile art for blocks, enemies, backgrounds, and the player — not plain ColorRect fills. Different depth tiers have visually distinct themes. Score 0 if environments are uniform color fills.

HUD and UI chrome: health display, gem counter, combo indicator, shop interface, and game-over screen use styled themed widgets — not raw unstyled HTML 引擎 defaults. Score 0 if primary UI elements are obviously unstyled.

Animation and feedback: shooting produces muzzle flash and recoil motion, enemies explode on death, combo counter pulses on increment, gems sparkle, and the shop has transition animations. Score 0 if all state changes snap silently.
